name: DIVERGENCE(server): private-use characters survive the browser, the server blanks them

divergences.desktop: QChar::isPrint is false for Co (private use), so the U+E000 markers are blanked to spaces and simplified() collapses them — the Go server's behavior, not the browser's

comment: browser strips \p{Cc}\p{Cf} only; Go sanitizeUpstreamText blanks every !unicode.IsPrint rune (private-use, unassigned) — server walkers must expect a space here

name: DIVERGENCE(server,pystencil): length caps count UTF-16 code units in the browser, runes elsewhere

divergences.desktop: QChar::isPrint is false for Cs (surrogate halves), so every astral-plane emoji is blanked to two spaces and simplified() leaves "" — no cap even applies
divergences.mcp: counts chars (Unicode scalar values): 120 emoji = 120 chars, under the 200 cap, so the text passes whole — no surrogate split, no truncation

comment: browser String.slice can even split a surrogate pair at the 199-code-unit cut (the expect ends in a lone high surrogate); Go/Python count code points, Zig counts bytes — non-browser walkers must recompute their own expectation for astral input
